chunks: Ali, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The first of what God will judge concerning on the Day of Resurrection is bloodshed. He will stop the two sons of Adam and decide between them. Then those who followed them among the perpetrators of bloodshed, until none of them remains. Then the rest of the people after that, until the murdered one comes with his murderer, his face dripping in his blood, and he says: "This one killed me." So He will say: "Did you kill him?" And he will not be able to conceal any matter from God.'

key_terms.ابْنَيْ آدَم: The two sons of Adam — referring to Cain (Qabil) and Abel (Habil), the first murderer and first victim in Islamic tradition
key_terms.الدِّمَاء: Bloodshed, blood cases — the plural of dam (blood), referring here specifically to homicide
key_terms.يَتَشَخَّب: To be soaked/dripping — a vivid term describing blood-soaked appearance, reinforcing the tangible reality of the crime in the afterlife
key_terms.يَكْتُمَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثاً: Conceal any matter from God — emphasizing divine omniscience and the impossibility of escaping accountability

ai.seo_question: What is the first matter God will judge on the Day of Resurrection according to hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) transmits this saying of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) that on the Day of Resurrection, God will begin His judgment with cases of bloodshed. The hadith begins with the paradigmatic case of Cain and Abel — the two sons of Adam — and then proceeds through all subsequent cases of murder. The vivid imagery of the murdered one arriving with his face drenched in blood, pointing to his killer, emphasizes the certainty of divine justice and the impossibility of concealment before God. This hadith is situated in a jurisprudential context (Kitab al-Diyat, the Book of Blood Money) to underscore the gravity of taking a human life.
